analysis.title: 2027 Investment Outlook: The price of power
key_insights: Amundi frames 2027 around five powers (policy, capital, technology, energy, pricing). It expects global GDP growth of 3.3%, with US supported by productivity, Europe hit by the energy shock but helped by German fiscal stimulus, China split, and India above 7%.

Scenario probabilities: base 'uneven resilience' 60%, downside 'stress from vulnerabilities' 25%, upside 'AI and reform dividend' 10%, tail 'compound geopolitical rupture' 5%. Inflation stays above targets but eases through the year, with synchronised tightening peaking in Q1.

Fixed income: attractive entry points, but favour short to intermediate maturities first (especially eurozone and UK) and extend duration selectively later in 2027. Term premia and heavy sovereign issuance are the main upside risks to yields.

Credit: prefer investment grade over high yield because of refinancing and dispersion risks. EM debt is a core conviction, favouring selective local-currency debt (Brazil, Colombia, Hungary) and connector economies (India, Indonesia, Mexico, Kazakhstan).

Euro sovereigns: Italy and Spain supported by improving fundamentals, France offers entry points once political risk normalises. Low-debt govies such as Norway, Australia and Switzerland are favoured in the allocation sketch.

Portfolio construction moves from 60/40 to an illustrative 40/30/20/10: 40% equities, 30% fixed income and liquidity, 20% private and alternatives, 10% commodities. Real and alternative assets, commodities, gold and liquidity should be about 30% of allocations.

AI shifts from build-out to return scrutiny. Hyperscaler FCF is likely to trough in 2027 with capex above operating cash flow, and the build-out is increasingly debt-financed. IT is expected to supply 70% of MSCI ACWI net income growth in 2027, versus about 40% in 2026.

AI equity positioning: own bottlenecks (power equipment, grid, networking, chip fabrication) and AI facilitators (IT services and software). Be cautious on spending-dependent names (neoclouds, data centre developers, colocation REITs). Add dividends and valuation support, since high-dividend indices cushioned past tech drawdowns.
China's open-weight models and efficiency gains are flagged as the risk that challenges the AI returns thesis itself, not just its timing.

Macro regime is investment-led with weak consumption. Profits are outpacing labour compensation, the US consumer is reliant on top-income households and exposed to an equity correction, and persistent (not accelerating) inflation limits central bank easing. Financial repression risk rises with high debt and rates above growth.

FX: USD has near-term cyclical support from a possible hawkish Fed but faces structural pressure from fiscal concerns. Favour carry in AUD, NOK and GBP, EUR and CHF as funding currencies, and JPY as a diversifier.

Commodities: gold targeted above $5,000. Oil carries about a $20/bbl geopolitical risk premium with normalisation to a $70-80 range by end-2027 delayed. European gas is expected above €50/MWh through 2027. Copper demand is seen rising from 28Mt (2025) to 42Mt (2040), with selective copper producer exposure favoured.

Equity regional views: cautious on the S&P 500 but positive on equal-weight, Europe supported by fiscal stimulus and valuations, Japan constructive, EM constructive but selective, China neutral, India supportive, LatAm positive, Pacific ex Japan unattractive.

Sector views: financials strongly preferred across regions, industrials favoured (especially Europe and Japan), utilities a preferred defensive hedge in US and Europe, consumer discretionary negative in Europe and Japan, real estate negative in US and Europe.

Alternatives: private assets favour infrastructure (Core+/value-add), senior secured and European mid-market direct lending, and secondaries. Hedge funds favour fundamental L/S equity, discretionary macro and flexible event-driven. EU direct lending offers a 25-100bps spread premium over the US.

Regional macro: BoJ expected to hike 25bp quarterly to a 2% terminal rate, China growth target seen cut to around 4.5%, India growth around 7% with a possible RBI hike, Brazil stagflationary pressures, Mexico recovering with possible Banxico cut in early 2027.

sector_views.rationale: High distribution yield and still reasonable valuations, rated ++ in US and + in Europe and Japan.
Government spending and private sector capex, ++ in Europe and Japan.
Preferred defensive hedge with decent earnings and peaking yields (US and Europe).
Selective exposure via semis in Europe and software in the US.
Structural challenges in autos, negative in Europe and Japan.
Weak relative earnings across the board.
Weak earnings trend and expensive in the US.
A play on the geopolitical situation.
Persistent weakness in Chinese demand limits upside.

earnings_insights: MSCI ACWI earnings breadth is improving, with more constituents expected to deliver higher net income in 2027 than in 2026 (forecast). IT is expected to account for 70% of index net income growth in 2027 versus about 40% in 2026, led by semiconductors and hardware.
Energy and communication services are expected to detract from 2027 net income growth, and consumer discretionary to contribute only modestly (forecast).
Japan earnings growth is expected to reach double digits in 2027 (forecast). Pacific ex Japan earnings growth is lagging.
US hyperscaler FCF is expected to trough in 2027 with capex above operating cash flow (forecast).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Resilient but divergent growth, driven by investment more than consumption.
Strong growth with rising external constraints.
Above target, RBI may hike late 2026 or early 2027.
Leadership tolerant of slower growth, stimulus kept in reserve.
Pre-emptive tightening supports JPY and Japan duration if a hawkish catalyst arrives.
Central bank buying and geopolitics offset higher rates.
Convergence delayed by geopolitical risk premium of about $20/bbl.
Europe's structural energy vulnerability keeps inflation pressure.

crypto_views: Stablecoin reserve requirements are cited as a possible form of regulation creating captive demand for government debt, a financial repression channel.

trade_ideas.description: Long gold, targeting above $5,000 over the next year
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong central bank buying, limited mine supply and geopolitical backdrop.

trade_ideas.description: Long carry FX in AUD, NOK and GBP funded in EUR and CHF
trade_ideas.rationale: Rate differentials and improving domestic fundamentals.
trade_ideas.risk: A hawkish Fed could extend USD support.

trade_ideas.description: Short-dated bonds first in eurozone and UK, extending duration selectively later in 2027
trade_ideas.rationale: Term premia and heavy issuance pressure long-end yields before they improve.
trade_ideas.risk: Faster rate declines or yield rally would leave duration underweight.

risk_factors: Funding squeeze and rising term premia amid heavy sovereign and AI-related issuance.
Debt-financed AI capex with falling free cash flow and returns that disappoint.
Renewed energy shock delaying monetary easing and re-accelerating inflation.
Geopolitical escalation or cyber event (compound rupture, 5% probability).
Leverage in non-banks and private credit, with liquidity mismatches.
US equity concentration and valuation, with consumer exposed to an equity correction.
Disorderly repricing from a policy mistake or unfunded fiscal announcement, hitting the long end first.
Physical AI constraints: power shortages, grid bottlenecks, packaging limits, permitting delays.
charts_described: Chart on p.10 plots hyperscaler capex, free cash flow and net debt in $ bln from 2015 to 2028, per the title that capex is increasingly debt-funded.
Chart on p.20 shows average monthly return vs USD when US real yields rise and inflation breakevens fall, with NOK and AUD at -1.6% each and EUR at -0.6%.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility is expected to stay elevated, with policy instability and momentum-driven flows keeping markets fragile.
USD positioning is described as stretched with rich valuations.
Hedging should be part of portfolio design, but no single hedge fits all scenarios. Gold, strategic commodities, JPY and cash are favoured for stress scenarios.
Dividends cushioned MSCI World Tech drawdowns of more than 10% in episodes from Dec 2022 through Autumn 2026.
Leverage in non-bank financials and private credit, and repo and Treasury intermediation dependence, are flagged as instability sources.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict disrupted energy markets and lifted energy prices, creating a persistent oil risk premium.
Ukraine conflict: a ceasefire is an upside driver while expansion to NATO countries is a flagged surprise risk.
Seminar respondents named resolution of the Iran conflict and weakening of US institutions among the top geopolitical surprises.
US-China AI split into a US-led network under Pax Silica and a Chinese self-sufficiency ecosystem, with export controls on advanced compute.
China controls more than 90% of refining for some critical minerals.
Brazil's 'no regime change' election outcome hit sentiment, and Japan's LDP lower-house supermajority supports policy stability.

tension_points.bull_case: Cycle is maturing with further to run: equity issuance below past excesses, richer hyperscaler monetisation levers, and external financing still below real estate and utilities thanks to high operating cash flows.
tension_points.bear_case: Leverage and off-balance-sheet commitments are rising, FCF is thinning, and a gap between capital deployed and returns could widen as financing costs rise.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Any wavering on spending guidance or disappointing earnings from hyperscalers, which risks a sharp re-rating of the AI infrastructure complex.

tension_points.bull_case: US 10-year yields are approaching historically attractive levels, offering entry points for long-term investors.
tension_points.bear_case: AI investment, heavy issuance and renewed inflation risk could push real yields and term premia higher first.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A renewed energy shock that challenges inflation expectations and delays monetary easing.

theme_stances.key_argument: The narrative shifts from who invests most to who captures highest returns, favouring bottleneck owners and facilitators over spending-dependent names.
theme_stances.evidence: the narrative is shifting from who can invest the most to who can capture the highest returns

theme_stances.key_argument: Fiscal pressures and competition for capital favour short to intermediate bonds initially with gradual extension.
theme_stances.evidence: favour a gradual extension of duration rather than an immediate shift to long-term bonds
